title: Measure what the two records carry and what no record carries

whereAGraphReachesARecord.description: The only place a signal graph reaches a record: the serializer, and the one field of a per-check record that carries its result.

recordedShape.description: The shape a reader accepts: an object with a `nodes` list and an `edges` list, nodes keyed by a numeric `index`, edges keyed by the two index ends.
recordedShape.shape: { nodes: [{ index, kind, label, … }], edges: [{ consumer, producer }] }

ignored: any cause a later capture might add
node.note: Only `index`, `kind` and `label` of a node are read; a node carrying any other field changes nothing a reader reports.

edge.note: An edge is two members and nothing else: a direction of dependency, with no field, no value and no moment.

whatTheSerializerItselfWrites.description: Measured from the source: `serializeGraph` pushes nodes keyed by `id`, never by `index`, and resolves each edge end to the consumer/producer node id rather than its index. So a record produced by this serializer carries no node `index` at all, and cannot feed a reader that reads `index`.

join.description: The render/effect entry: one function, one fact in, one answer out.

effectFinding.note: The effect finding has exactly four fields: the state, the effect label, how the caller named it, and the read list. No phase, no write, no owner, no cause.

readList.name: reads
readList.contents: the labels of the producer ends of the effect’s consumer edges, in the order the edges appear
rules: a producer the graph does not hold names nothing and is skipped
a producer whose label is empty names nothing and is skipped
no fallback, no borrowing, no sort — the recorded order is the only order

publishedAbsences.names: the effect node the readable graph lacks
the read list is built from the effect’s own index

neverMerged.description: The effect finding and a recorded change-detection message stay two findings in the recorded order, the effect first; the message is pushed after it and the two are never joined.

purity.description: The module reads what it is given and nothing else: no DOM, no clock, no console, no network, no imports, no page global beyond one namespace. A bare `node:vm` context runs it, and the capture belongs to a caller.

noEdgeCarriesAnOrderField.conclusion: An edge carries only `consumer` and `producer` (and, in derived readings, labels and a rendered `edge` string). No field, value or moment orders a write, so the ordering is a named absence and not a capture this milestone could add.

whatNoRecordCarriesInstead.description: What no record carries is the serialized shape: `serializeGraph` keys nodes by `id` and never by `index`, so no record the agent’s own serializer wrote carries a node index, and none of them can feed a reader that reads `index`. The graph in the recorded shape that does exist on disk is a capture (m039’s freshRead), not a serialized record.
whatNoRecordCarriesInstead.conclusion: The graph this milestone reads is a capture (T003) — the plan’s operative conclusion stands — but not for the reason the plan stated: records do carry effect nodes, one of them in the recorded shape with an index. The absence is of an `index` in the serializer’s own output.

inventory.measured: This recording measures no record under `research/raw/`: its 54 citations are lines of the join, the reader and the serializer, not another record's own claims, so the map it states is read over records the two inventories name rather than over records this file quotes.

M057's own verdict list, ruling the criteria the intent this milestone binds declares: T009 captured it after this map was measured, so it is named outside the map rather than read as an unmeasured record — the same subtraction T004's own map made for M055's verdict list and its surface record, which is the mechanism the two inventories apply.
